petition_no: Review Petition No. 7 of 2026 & Review Petition No. 8 of 2026 & IA No. 1047 of 2026 In Original Petition No. 1 of 2025
summary: Counsel for the Petitioner(s) : B. P. Patil, Sr. Adv. Abiha Zaidi for Petitioner Counsel for the : Amit Kapur Respondent(s) Anupam Varma Rahul Kinra Aditya Ajay Aditya Gupta Girdhar Gopal Khattar Adamya Ojha Yash Srivastava Mahima Kaur for Res. 31 & 32 _3._ Mr. B.P. Patil, Learned Senior Counsel has referred to the orders dated 11[th] February, 2026 and 26[th] September, 2025 passed by this Tribunal in the original petition with regards to the Delhi Commission to submit that this Tribunal, in these orders, had not barred or declined the move of the Commission to conduct strict and intensive audit of Delhi Discoms by CAG and also directed the Commission to submit progressive report regarding such action thereby permitting the Commission to get such audit conducted by CAG and, therefore, the order dated 20[th] April, 2026 upholding the objection of Discoms to such audit and quashing the approval accorded by the Lt. Governor to such audit suffers from manifest error and therefore deserves to be reviewed on this aspect. _4._ The relevant portions of the orders dated 11[th] February, 2026 and 26[th] September, 2025 , to which the Learned Senior Counsel had referred, have been extracted in para No. 4 & 5 of the application and we find it pertinent to extract those portions of these two orders hereunder also :- _this regard to this Tribunal by way of a progress report before the next date of hearing.”_ 5. It is limpid that in the order dated 11[th] February, 2026, this Tribunal observed that the objection of Delhi Discom that CAG audit is impressible, cannot be readily brushed aside, but refrained from examining this contention as no auditor had been appointed till that date by the Commission. In the subsequent order dated 26[th] September, 2025 this Tribunal has merely recorded the submission on behalf of the Commission that they have approached CAG to undertake the special audit of the Delhi Discoms and the assurance that in case no response/or refusal from CAG, they shall initiate steps to appoint auditors on their own. 6. Hence, there is nothing in these two orders to show or suggest that this Tribunal approved the action of the Commission to entrust the special audit of the Discoms to CAG, and thus, the interpretation which is sought to be given on behalf of the Commission is absolutely erroneous. Deriving of such conclusion by the Commission from these two orders of this Tribunal appears to be patently fallacious and pre-posterous. have to do so itself. Such course of action adopted by this Tribunal was held impermissible by the Hon’ble Supreme Court on the ground that Section 121 does not give any power to the Tribunal to decide any dispute pending before the regulatory Commissions and only empowers this Tribunal to, after hearing the concerned Commission as well as other interested parties, issue orders/instructions or directions to the Commission for performance of its statutory functions. That is not the case herein. No such dispute involving the Delhi Discom is pending before the Commission. The Commission had, in pursuance to RA judgement dated 6[th] August, 2025 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court proceeded to conduct special audit of Delhi Discoms by CAG for which approval was accorded by the Lt. Governor vide communication dated 5[th] March, 2026 but objection was raised by Delhi Discoms to such audit before this Tribunal. This Tribunal has been monitoring the conducting of intensive audit of discoms by the Regulatory Commissions throughout India in terms of the said judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Therefore, we have noted in para No. 36 of the order that it is implicit in the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court to this Tribunal to monitor the directions contained in paragraph No. 71 of the RA judgement that this Tribunal 8. Hence, the contention on behalf of the Delhi Commission that the order dated 20[th] April, 2026 of this Tribunal in this original petition suffers from any error on the face of the record appears to be only figment of imagination of the Commission itself which is not borne out from the meaningful perusal of the said order. The contentions are absolutely fallacious and mis-conceived to say the least. 11. By way of this petition, the Delhi Commission has sought review/recall/modification of the order dated 20[th] April, 2026 to the extent it rejects the request of the Commission for commencing process of liquidation of regulatory assets w.e.f. 1[st] July, 2026. Further direction of this Tribunal to commence process of liquidation of regulatory assets within three weeks from 20[th] April, 2026 is also sought to be recalled/modified. order and have been repelled by the observations contained in paragraph Nos. 48 & 49 of the order. Therefore, by way of the instant petition, the Commission only seeks fresh consideration on these contentions which is not permissible. There may be appropriate remedies available to the Commission in case it is not satisfied with such directions passed by us in the order dated 20[th] April, 2026. However, certainly the instant petition does not make out any ground for review/recall/modification of the said order. 13. We are constrained to note that considering the statutory procedure to be followed for issue of true-up order, as was conveyed to us during the hearing on 20[th] April, 2026, we had granted time to the Commission till 30[th] June, 2026 for passing true up order for Financial Year 2023-24. We hope and expect that the said true up order would be passed by the Commission on or before the said specified date. However, as we have noted in the order dated 20[th] April, 2026, there is no impediment as such in the way of the Commission in commencing the process of liquidation of regulatory assets of the Discoms.
